scope: External code references for literal cross-game ports and bridges. These are not complete openly licensed games, hosted builds, partnerships or verified installations. Each requires separately supplied original games/assets. Follow creator licences, compatibility and offline-use requirements.

projects.title: Mario 64 inside Elden Ring
projects.creator: deltarooo and contributors
projects.summary: A real movement and character integration: libsm64 runs Mario against Elden Ring’s collision, with a native mod connecting the systems.
projects.requiredGames: Your own Elden Ring install and compatible US Super Mario 64 ROM. Game data is not included or licensed by the mod.
projects.requirements: Experimental Windows/native mod. Follow the original offline-only instructions and separate-save guidance.
projects.aiRole: No AI-authorship claim found in the reviewed README.

projects.title: Minecraft inside Skyrim
projects.creator: chasmlol and contributors
projects.summary: Runs both games and connects them through a Skyrim plugin, Minecraft mod and shared memory, bringing blocks and Minecraft systems into Skyrim.
projects.requiredGames: Your own Skyrim Special/Anniversary Edition and Minecraft Java entitlement. Neither game is included.
projects.requirements: Experimental native Windows setup with SKSE, Fabric and additional tools. Read the original compatibility and resource requirements.
projects.aiRole: No AI-authorship claim found in the reviewed README.

projects.title: Minecraft inside GTA V
projects.creator: rehan-remade and Universal Modder contributors
projects.summary: A Minecraft/GTA bridge example using game-side plugins, shared state and depth compositing while both games run.
projects.codeLicense: MIT framework and example code; retain component notices
projects.requiredGames: Your own compatible Minecraft Java and GTA V installs. No GTA or Minecraft game data is provided by Game Commons.
projects.requirements: Complex experimental native toolchain; the creator documents GTA Story Mode/offline use. This is an external source reference, not a browser player.
projects.aiRole: The example README explicitly credits Claude Code; that is the creator’s disclosure, not an independent authorship audit.
